title: Best Bank Statement Fraud Detection Software
summary: Bank statement fraud detection software compared for lenders and KYB teams: file forensics, statement analysis, and when a bank connection wins.
body_markdown:
**TL;DR:** Bank statement fraud detection software comes in three forms: forensic tools that test the submitted file, statement analysis tools that add fraud signals to extracted data, and bank connections that avoid the file altogether. Most lenders, underwriters and KYB teams need a connection where the applicant can link and a file check everywhere else. The stakes are concrete: in a[January 2025 Justice Department case](https://www.fhfaoig.gov/sites/default/files/Hampton-Woman-Pleads-Guilty-to-%24161-Million-Mortgage-Fraud-Scheme.pdf) , a defendant admitted altering or fabricating bank statements, pay stubs and W-2s behind about 450 mortgage loans totaling roughly $161 million.


Sphinx wrote this list. The numbering is an order of fit for teams that receive statements as files, not an independent ranking. Every product here publicly describes bank statement checks or bank data for lending, and vendor details come from each company's own pages and press as of November 2026.


## Three tools answer three different questions


The category name hides a real split: buyers comparing these products are often comparing answers to different questions.


Document forensics asks whether this file is what it claims to be. It reads how the PDF was produced and changed, and whether the page behaves like that bank's statement. Statement analysis asks what the file says and whether it adds up, then turns transactions into underwriting numbers, with fraud signals alongside. A bank connection asks what is in the account, using data the applicant permissions from the institution.


Each one leaves something out. Forensics does not tell you the true balance. Analysis tools can inherit a forger's clean arithmetic. A connection fails the moment an applicant declines or the bank is not supported, and it says nothing about a forged file the applicant already sent you.


The manual tells are a separate subject, covered in[how to spot a fake bank statement](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/how-to-spot-a-fake-bank-statement) . This post is about what to buy. If your team is still deciding whether it needs authenticity checks or data verification at all,[document verification versus document fraud detection](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/document-verification-vs-document-fraud-detection) draws that line first.

## Eight options, in order of fit


### 1. Sphinx — Best for lender and KYB teams that want an evidenced verdict on each file


Sphinx Doc Fraud runs six checks on a file: production method, timestamp trail, issuer matching, consistency, model artifacts and recycled patterns. Each result includes an evidence x-ray. Sphinx reports a 94.3% correct verdict and under 28 seconds to clear clean files. At a $30B+ US bank, 91% of documents cleared and 17% more fraud was caught. Pricing is $0.45 per document, and teams can[test their own files in the free playground](https://sphinxhq.com/products/doc-fraud) first.


Doc Fraud also runs inside KYB and KYC review, where Sphinx prepares the evidence, applies your SOPs, and produces a traceable recommendation; your team retains final approval. The limit follows from reading files: Sphinx does not connect to the bank, confirm a balance with the issuer, or build a cash flow analysis.


### 2. Inscribe — Best for reviewing a whole application across its documents


Inscribe focuses on the financial documents that underwriting and onboarding teams see most: bank statements, pay stubs and tax forms. It describes four detection layers (forensic, network, semantic and perceptual), and says it reasons across an application rather than one document at a time, with an assistant that answers follow-up questions about findings. Each finding carries a risk level and a description. Banks, credit unions, lenders and fintechs are its stated audience, and teams with multi-document applications are the natural fit.


The limit is commercial rather than technical. Pricing is custom by document volume across Base and Premium plans, and evaluation runs through a four-week pilot, so evaluation takes weeks rather than an afternoon.


### 3. Resistant AI — Best for any document type across many countries


Resistant Documents is built to be document-agnostic and language-agnostic. The company says it looks at how a document is built rather than what it says, returns verdicts of Trusted, Warning or High Risk with supporting evidence, and takes under 20 seconds per document. It reports training on more than 200 million documents. That design suits merchant onboarding or lending programs taking unfamiliar paperwork from many markets.


The same design sets the limit: reading structure rather than content means no underwriting numbers, so lenders pair it with an analysis tool. Buyers should also know that since October 2026 Resistant AI's engine has powered the forensic layer in Ocrolus Detect, so those two entries are not fully independent options.


### 4. Ocrolus Detect — Best for lenders wanting extraction, analytics and fraud signals together


Ocrolus is a lending platform specializing in bank statements, pay stubs and tax forms, with cash flow and income analytics as its core. Detect adds an authenticity score from 0 to 100, High, Medium or Low status, and reason codes. Its docs describe two signal sources: Ocrolus's own checks on whether balances, totals and dates add up, and Resistant AI's file and pixel forensics. A separate product, Docs-to-Digital, reconciles PDF statements against Plaid, Finicity or Decision Logic data and scores each mismatch by severity. In October 2026 Ocrolus made Detect available at no added cost to its mortgage customers.


Detect makes the most sense for a lender already processing files through Ocrolus. It is built around lending, not KYB, and its docs list serial fraud and template reuse detection as coming in early 2027.


### 5. MoneyThumb Thumbprint — Best for MCA funders and small-business lenders


Thumbprint scores each PDF statement from 1 to 1,000 and lists the factors behind the score, typically in under five seconds. Two models run: one checks whether the statement agrees with itself on fonts, spacing, dates and balances, the other compares it with verified statements from the same bank. MoneyThumb says this holds up after a file is re-saved or scrubbed because it does not rely on metadata. Scores arrive in the platform or by webhook, and it runs alongside MoneyThumb's PDF Insights analysis. Plans start at $599.95 a year, one of the few public prices in this category.


The score is an input, and your team sets the thresholds and owns what happens next. The same-bank comparison also depends on a reference library, so test it on the small banks and credit unions in your own book.


### 6. DocuClipper — Best for small underwriting and forensic teams working full statement sets


DocuClipper treats a loan file or case as a set of statements. A coverage grid flags missing months, each statement is added up from its printed opening balance to its printed closing balance, and every PDF gets a 0 to 100 authenticity score with reasons. It also pairs transfers between a borrower's own accounts and surfaces accounts referenced but never produced. Plans are priced by pages with unlimited users, and a 14-day trial with no credit card covers up to 120 pages.


DocuClipper states plainly that the score is a guide and not a verdict, and a reviewer confirms each flag.


### 7. Plaid — Best for permissioned bank data and bank-sourced statement copies


Plaid sidesteps the file. With the applicant's permission, it returns balances, identity and transaction history from the institution. Plaid says it connects to over 12,000 institutions, and in May 2025 reported business account support at 95% of US banks serving small businesses. Its Statements product, US only, retrieves an exact bank-branded PDF directly from the bank, up to two years back. Plaid's docs point most new US lending customers to Consumer Report by Plaid Check, its FCRA-covered product, and Plaid Assets is a Day 1 Certainty report supplier for Fannie Mae's Desktop Underwriter.


The limit is the link itself. The applicant has to complete it, the institution has to support the product requested, and a linked account does not tell you whether a PDF already in the file was genuine.


### 8. Mastercard Open Finance — Best for US lenders wanting FCRA-covered asset and income reports


Mastercard Open Finance, which includes Finicity, offers Verification of Assets, Verification of Income, Cash Flow Analytics and a Statements product that retrieves bank statements as PDFs, all from customer-permissioned data. Mastercard cites 95% coverage of US demand deposit accounts and a history in mortgage. Its docs describe Finicity as a registered consumer reporting agency, and a separate business lending offering sits alongside the consumer reports. That profile fits mortgage, auto and personal lenders.


The limit matches Plaid's: everything depends on the customer connecting an account, and the core asset report operations list the US as the supported region, so cross-border KYB programs need another route.


## When connecting to the bank beats checking the file


A bank connection beats a file check whenever the applicant can link, because the question changes from "is this document real" to "what does the bank say." That matters most for high-value credit, asset verification and any decision that hinges on a current balance. Connections also keep working after approval, since lenders can refresh data without asking for new documents. Where a connection is available, make it the default.


The file check takes over in four situations:


- The applicant declines to link, or the institution or product is not supported.
- The account sits outside the provider's market. Plaid Statements, for one, is US only.
- The file already exists: a broker package, a KYB onboarding folder, or a back-book review.
- The person applying cannot link the account. Plaid's help center notes that at Bank of America, only the main account holder's username can link a business account.


KYB teams should weigh that last point. The CFPB's personal financial data rights rule[defines a consumer as a natural person](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-X/part-1033/subpart-A/section-1033.131) , so it should not be read as a guarantee of access to business accounts. Its consumer timeline is unsettled too: the[CFPB's compliance page](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/compliance/compliance-resources/other-applicable-requirements/personal-financial-data-rights/) records that a court stayed the compliance dates on October 29, 2025, and the agency is reconsidering the rule. For now, access depends on aggregator coverage and applicant consent.


A connection also leaves two gaps. Dropping the document discards a signal, because an applicant who submitted a forged statement and then linked a thin account has told you something that matters for the case record. The second gap is ownership: data from a linked account proves little until someone confirms the account belongs to the applicant, which is why both Plaid and Mastercard sell account-owner checks. Staged deposits in a real account remain an underwriter's judgment call whichever tool you use.


Many programs land on both: connection first, forensic check as the fallback, and reconciliation when both exist. A mismatch between PDF and connection still needs an explanation before anyone acts on it, since periods and accounts can differ innocently.


## How to pick without a sales call


Start with where your statements come from. Loan files arriving through brokers, or[packages reviewed as a set](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/loan-document-fraud-detection) , favor file checks that run on everything. Direct digital applicants can usually be offered a connection first. For onboarding, statements sit beside registry documents, so[KYB document fraud](https://sphinxhq.com/blog-posts/kyb-document-fraud-detection) tends to need a tool that handles more than one document type.


Then work through these questions:


1. Does it test edited real statements as well as generated ones? Ask for results on each separately.
2. What comes back: a verdict, a score, or a flag? Someone has to own the threshold, and a score with no reasons leaves your analyst to rebuild the case.
3. What happens with a screenshot or phone photo, where file history is gone?
4. Can a reviewer defend the result months later?
5. Does it need the underwriting numbers too? If yes, an analysis tool or a pairing beats a forensic tool alone.
6. What will it cost at your real volume, including minimums and platform fees?


Then run a break test. Pull a sample from your own book, mix in confirmed fakes and clean files from your small banks and credit unions, and score every vendor on the same set. Vendor accuracy figures are self-reported, Sphinx's included, and come from different mixes of documents. Free tiers and trials make that cheap: Sphinx's playground and DocuClipper's trial need no card, and Inscribe's pilot is designed around your sample.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is bank statement fraud detection software?


Bank statement fraud detection software checks whether a submitted statement is genuine, using signals such as how the file was produced, whether it was changed after creation, whether it matches the issuing bank's format, and whether the numbers reconcile. Some products also extract transactions for underwriting, while bank connections replace the file with data from the institution.


### Is open banking better than checking the PDF?


Open banking gives a stronger answer about the account when the applicant can link, because the data comes from the institution rather than a document the applicant controlled. It does not help when the applicant declines, the institution is unsupported, or the file was collected earlier. A connection as the default with a file check as the fallback covers both cases.


### Can software detect an AI-generated bank statement?


Several vendors on this list, including Sphinx, Inscribe, Resistant AI and Ocrolus, describe checks for AI-generated documents. No vendor's claim should be accepted without testing, since detection varies by generator and by how the file was saved afterward. Include generated samples in your break test and score them separately from edited real statements.


### How much does bank statement fraud detection software cost?


Public pricing is uneven. Sphinx Doc Fraud is $0.45 per document, MoneyThumb plans start at $599.95 a year, and DocuClipper prices by pages. Inscribe prices by document volume on a custom quote, and Resistant AI lists no price on its own site. Compare cost at your actual monthly volume.


### Do KYB teams need different software than lenders?


Often, yes. Lenders usually want statement checks tied to underwriting numbers, while KYB teams review a statement next to registry filings, ownership documents and proof of address, so coverage across document types matters more than cash flow analytics. Bank connections can also be harder in KYB, because the person handling onboarding may not be able to link the business account.
